reports.title: BPS – Statistics Indonesia (Badan Pusat Statistik)
reports.description: The national statistical office of Indonesia. Responsible for censuses, surveys, and the large majority of official socio-economic statistics. Publishes an extensive catalogue of recurring series and the annual Statistical Yearbook of Indonesia.
reports._notes: Institutional core node. Every subsequent BPS series will reference this authority.
_referenced_by: All major BPS statistical programmes and the Statistical Yearbook
National planning documents (RPJMN) and policy analysis that cite official data

reports.title: Statistical Yearbook of Indonesia (Statistik Indonesia)
reports.description: Flagship annual compendium presenting geographic, demographic, social and economic statistics drawn from BPS and other agencies. Provides national and provincial comparisons and technical notes. Continuously cited as the single-volume overview of official Indonesian statistics.
reports._notes: Highest-visibility recurring BPS product. Functions as the ‘one-stop’ official statistical reference.
_referenced_by: Policy documents, academic work and international reports that need a comprehensive official snapshot
Provincial statistical yearbooks that mirror its structure

reports.title: Population Census (Sensus Penduduk) and Long Form results
reports.description: Decennial population census (most recent full cycle SP2020 with short-form enumeration and subsequent Long Form survey). Produces the definitive population stock, fertility, mortality, migration and related demographic parameters used throughout the statistical system.
reports._notes: Foundational demographic node. The Long Form SP2020 results are the current high-detail source for fertility, mortality and migration.
_referenced_by: Labour-force, education, health and poverty surveys that use census frames
National Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMN) population targets

reports.title: National Accounts / GDP statistics (PDB)
reports.description: Quarterly and annual national accounts (Produk Domestik Bruto) by expenditure and by industrial origin, at current and constant prices. Provincial GDP (PDRB) series exist and will be densified later.
reports._notes: Core macro node. Provincial PDRB will form the main spatial economic layer in later batches.
_referenced_by: Bank Indonesia Economic Report on Indonesia

reports.title: Consumer Price Index (Indeks Harga Konsumen – IHK)
reports.description: Monthly Consumer Price Index and inflation rates. Compiled for a set of cities and aggregated to national urban inflation. Primary inflation indicator used by Bank Indonesia and the government.
reports._notes: High-frequency price node. Directly linked to monetary policy and poverty measurement.
_referenced_by: Bank Indonesia monetary-policy decisions and reports
Poverty line calculations and real-income analysis

reports.title: National Labour Force Survey (Sakernas)
reports.description: Periodic labour-force survey producing employment, unemployment, underemployment, labour-force participation and informal-sector indicators. Principal official source for labour-market statistics.
reports._cadence_original: multiple rounds per year (frequency has varied; currently high-frequency)
reports._notes: Core labour node. Critical for understanding the large informal sector and youth employment challenges.
_referenced_by: Bank Indonesia and fiscal assessments of the real economy

reports.title: Poverty statistics (official poverty line and incidence)
reports.description: Official poverty measurement using the basic-needs poverty line (food + non-food). Published at national and provincial level, with urban/rural splits. Continuously cited in RPJMN targets and social-protection design.
reports._notes: High-policy-visibility social node. Provincial poverty rates will be important for later regional densification.

reports.title: National Socio-Economic Survey (Susenas)
reports.description: Large-scale household survey that is the primary source for consumption, expenditure, poverty calculation, education, health and many SDG indicators. Conducted in multiple modules and rounds.
reports._notes: Foundational household microdata node that underpins poverty, inequality and many social statistics.

reports.title: Bank Indonesia – central bank statistical and policy publications
reports.description: Central bank of Indonesia. Publishes monetary statistics, balance of payments, financial-system statistics (SSKI), the Economic Report on Indonesia (LPI), Financial Stability Review, and multiple surveys (business, banking, property).
reports._notes: Second institutional pillar alongside BPS. Will generate multiple detailed series in subsequent batches.

reports.title: Economic Report on Indonesia (Laporan Perekonomian Indonesia – LPI)
reports.description: Bank Indonesia’s flagship annual economic report. Reviews domestic and external performance, monetary and financial developments, and policy outlook. Continuously cited as the authoritative central-bank narrative.
reports._notes: High-authority annual narrative node from the central bank.
_referenced_by: International assessments of the Indonesian economy

reports.title: Indonesia Financial System Statistics (SSKI)
reports.description: Monthly compilation of financial-system indicators covering banks, non-bank financial institutions, financial markets, payment systems, and related real-sector linkages. Core macroprudential data product.
reports._notes: High-frequency financial-system node.

reports.title: Balance of Payments and International Investment Position
reports.description: Standard BPM-based balance-of-payments and IIP statistics. Key external-sector series for a commodity-exporting and capital-flow-sensitive economy.
reports._notes: Core external-sector node.

reports.title: Strait of Malacca — strategic chokepoint and transit statistics/context
reports.publisher: Derived from international maritime/energy analyses + Indonesian sovereignty context (Sumatra side)
reports.description: The primary western gateway between the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea / Pacific. Handles a very large share of global maritime trade and an even larger share of seaborne energy flows from the Middle East and Africa to East Asia. Indonesia controls a significant portion of the southern coastline. Continuously cited in energy-security, shipping and geopolitical analysis.
reports._notes: Highest-centrality maritime-chokepoint node for Indonesia. Critical for understanding why the archipelago sits at the centre of Asian energy security.

reports.title: Sunda Strait — alternative passage statistics/context
reports.publisher: Derived from maritime and Indonesian official context
reports.description: Major alternative route between the Indian Ocean and the Java Sea / internal Indonesian waters. Shallower and more constrained than Lombok; used as a partial substitute when Malacca is stressed. Fully under Indonesian sovereignty.
reports._notes: Key alternative-passage node under full Indonesian control.

reports.title: Lombok and Makassar Straits — deep-water alternative passages
reports.publisher: Derived from maritime analyses + Indonesian sovereignty
reports.description: Deep-water alternative routes preferred by the largest deep-draft tankers and bulk carriers (especially when Malacca draft is limiting) and by traffic linked to Australia. Also strategically relevant for submarine transit. Entirely within Indonesian archipelagic waters.
reports._notes: Deep-water redundancy nodes that raise Indonesia’s strategic maritime centrality.
_referenced_by: Australian and East Asian trade-route studies

reports.title: Indonesian Archipelagic Sea Lanes (ALKI) and archipelagic-state regime
reports.description: The formal Archipelagic Sea Lanes (ALKI) designated under the archipelagic-state regime of UNCLOS. Legal and operational frame that governs transit through Indonesian waters while preserving sovereignty. Recurring citation in maritime policy, defence and international-law contexts.
reports._notes: Foundational legal-regime node for all Indonesian chokepoint and transit analysis.
_referenced_by: Malacca, Sunda, Lombok and Makassar nodes

reports.title: Inter-provincial / inter-regional trade statistics (Perdagangan Antar Wilayah)
reports.description: Official BPS publication on inter-provincial trade — purchases and sales of goods between provinces, trade maps, and modes of transport. Captures the domestic commercial circulation that links Java, Sumatra, Kalimantan, Sulawesi, Papua and the other islands.
reports._notes: Core domestic-commerce node. Shows that Indonesia is not only an international transit state but also a complex internal trading system across thousands of islands.

reports.title: Inter-island trade volume and value (selected commodity series)
reports.description: Statistics on inter-island movements of food crops and other commodities. Complements the broader inter-provincial trade publication with commodity-specific domestic flow data.
reports._notes: Commodity-flow densification of the domestic-trade cluster.
reports._url_evidence: BPS page confirms 'Perdagangan Antar Wilayah Indonesia 2024', on inter-provincial purchases and sales with trade maps and transport modes.

reports.title: Special Economic Zones (KEK) statistics and regulatory framework
reports.publisher: Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs / KEK administration / related
reports.description: Regulatory framework and performance statistics for Indonesia’s Special Economic Zones (Kawasan Ekonomi Khusus). Includes tax holidays, customs facilities, VAT treatment and investment incentives designed to attract industry to designated locations across the archipelago.
reports._notes: Policy instrument that explicitly tries to shape industrial location across a diverse archipelago.

reports.title: Free Trade and Free Port Zones (KPBPB / FTZ) — Batam, Bintan, Karimun, Sabang
reports.publisher: Directorate General of Customs / related legal framework
reports.description: Free Trade and Free Port Zones with separate customs treatment (duty, VAT, excise relief). Batam–Bintan–Karimun form the principal FTZ complex facing Singapore and the Malacca approaches; Sabang is the western outlier. Legal basis in successive laws and implementing regulations.
reports._notes: Customs-and-tariff regime node that sits directly on the approaches to the Malacca Strait.
_referenced_by: Malacca Strait and Riau Islands regional analysis
reports._url_evidence: Retrieved the DJBC (Directorate General of Customs and Excise) regulation directory topic page 'Kawasan Perdagangan Bebas', which lists 14 instruments governing free trade and free port zones from UU 36/2000 (the founding law) through PMK-34/PMK.04/2021 and PMK-173/PMK.03/2021 on goods entry/exit and VAT treatment, up to PER-4/BC/2026. This is the customs legal framework for the KPBPB/FTZ regime. The DJBC content page beacukai.go.id/arsip/fas/fasilitas-kawasan-khusus.html still returns a 404 shell and bpbatam.go.id is still 403.
reports._url_route: alternate hostname on the same publisher - peraturan.beacukai.go.id serves static content where www.beacukai.go.id content paths 404

reports.title: Customs, tariff and trade-facilitation regime
reports.publisher: Directorate General of Customs and Excise / Ministry of Finance / Ministry of Trade
reports.description: The broader customs and tariff framework that governs both international and (indirectly) domestic trade. Includes preferential treatment under ASEAN, RCEP and bilateral arrangements, as well as the special regimes applied inside SEZs and FTZs.
reports._notes: Umbrella regulatory node for tariff and border treatment.
reports._url_evidence: Directorate General of Customs and Excise reference page confirmed to carry the Buku Tarif Kepabeanan Indonesia (BTKI) 2022 and customs tariff/exchange-rate references.

reports.title: Inter-island connectivity and logistics policy/statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from BPS transport statistics, Ministry of Transportation, and connectivity programmes
reports.description: Statistical and policy traces of inter-island shipping, port connectivity and logistics programmes intended to reduce price disparities and integrate the domestic market across the archipelago.
reports._notes: Domestic-integration counterpart to the international chokepoint nodes.

reports.title: Indonesia maritime-chokepoint, inter-provincial trade and special-zone meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from maritime, BPS trade, SEZ/FTZ and customs sources
reports.description: Meta-node that binds the Strait of Malacca, Sunda Strait, Lombok–Makassar passages, Archipelagic Sea Lanes regime, inter-provincial and inter-island trade statistics, Special Economic Zones, Free Trade/Free Port Zones, customs/tariff regime, and inter-island connectivity policy into a single high-centrality cluster. Captures both Indonesia’s role as a global energy and trade transit state and its internal commercial diversity across thousands of islands.
reports._notes: High-mass integrating node for the strategic-geography and internal-diversity layer requested by the user.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
Energy, trade, provincial and external-sector series from earlier batches

reports.title: Defence budget and military expenditure statistics
reports.publisher: Ministry of Defence / Ministry of Finance / international compilations citing official figures
reports.description: Official and widely cited defence budget allocations (recent figures rising toward Rp 187 trillion in 2026) and broader military-expenditure estimates. Defence burden remains relatively low as a share of GDP for an archipelagic state with extensive maritime interests.
reports._notes: Core defence-resource node. Links fiscal capacity to the maritime-strategic layer.
reports._url_evidence: Retrieved the Ministry of Finance publication 'Informasi APBN Tahun Anggaran 2025'. It contains the table '10 Kementerian/Lembaga dengan Pagu Terbesar pada APBN 2025' in which Kementerian Pertahanan appears fifth with Rp166.26 trillion. Also verified as a secondary route that the Ministry of Defence PPID does publish budget documents at https://ppid.kemhan.go.id/web/ppid/informasi-berkala (RKA 2021/2023/2024/2025, DIPA 2022/2023/2025, audited Laporan Keuangan 2020/2022/2024) - contrary to the earlier finding that it listed none.
reports._url_route: static asset host media.kemenkeu.go.id, bypassing the JS-only www.kemenkeu.go.id shell; kemhan PPID confirmed as a working backup

reports.title: Defence and security policy framing (archipelagic posture)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Defence / related strategic documents
reports.description: Recurring policy and strategic framing of Indonesia’s defence posture as an archipelagic state, including modernisation programmes and the linkage between territorial integrity, sea lanes and external security.
reports._notes: Policy-frame node that connects the defence cluster to the strategic-geography layer.
reports._url_evidence: PDF on the Ministry of Defence domain confirmed as Buku Putih Pertahanan Indonesia (Defence White Paper), setting out archipelagic defence doctrine and strategy.

reports.title: Statistics of Education
reports.description: Annual BPS education statistics covering process and outcome indicators from Susenas and administrative school data (schools, classrooms, teachers, sanitation). National and provincial presentation.

_variants.description: Official statistics on school enrolment, educational attainment, literacy and related indicators, largely drawn from Susenas and administrative sources.
_variants.notes: Human-capital node linked to the large youth population and skills agenda.
_variants.publisher: BPS – Statistics Indonesia / Ministry of Education related
_variants.title: Education statistics (enrolment, attainment, literacy)

reports._notes: Core education statistical product.
_referenced_by: Welfare Indicators and RPJMN human-development targets

reports.title: Gross Enrolment Ratio in tertiary education by province
reports.description: Provincial GER for tertiary education (age 19–23). Shows extreme variation — Yogyakarta far above the national average, eastern provinces much lower — reinforcing the spatial human-capital gradient.
reports._notes: High-visibility spatial education node (Yogyakarta outlier is especially notable).

reports.title: Construction in Figures / construction sector statistics
reports.description: Annual compilation of construction-sector data: workers, wages, construction value, materials, indices, construction GRDP, Construction Cost Index, etc. Provincial tables included.
reports._notes: Infrastructure and fixed-investment densification node.

reports.title: Paddy and rice production statistics by province
reports.publisher: BPS – Statistics Indonesia (Area Sampling Frame & crop-cutting surveys)
reports.description: Official harvested-area and production statistics for paddy (GKG) and rice. Java (especially East, West and Central) dominates production; the series is central to food-security and inflation analysis.
reports._notes: Foundational food-security production node. Strong Java concentration.

reports.title: Sea Transportation Statistics
reports.description: Annual statistics on ship calls, cargo loading/unloading, and passenger embarkation/disembarkation for domestic and international voyages at Indonesian seaports. Direct empirical counterpart to the inter-island and chokepoint layers.
reports._notes: Operational maritime-transport node that quantifies the domestic and international shipping activity through Indonesian ports.

reports.title: Domestic multimodal transport statistics (sea, air, rail, river/ferry)
reports.description: High-frequency and annual statistics on passenger and goods movement by sea, air, rail and river/lake/ferry modes. Captures the multi-modal character of mobility across the archipelago.
reports._notes: Broader mobility densification around the sea-transport core.

reports.title: Women and Men in Indonesia
reports.description: Annual gender-statistics compendium covering population, employment, health, education, housing, ICT and household socio-economic status for women and men.
reports._notes: Core gender-statistical product.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index of 38 Provinces
reports.description: Provincial CPI series (current base 2022=100) that reveal price-level and inflation differentials across the archipelago. Complements the national CPI and feeds analysis of inter-island price disparities.
reports._notes: Spatial price node that makes archipelagic price diversity statistically visible.

reports.title: Indonesia defence–education–construction–food–transport–gender densification meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from BPS, Ministry of Defence, Ministry of Finance and related sources
reports.description: Meta-node binding defence budget and archipelagic posture, education statistics and tertiary GER, construction sector statistics, paddy/rice production, sea and multimodal transport, gender statistics, and provincial CPI into a coherent multi-domain densification layer.
reports._notes: Integrating node for the multi-domain research rounds in Batch 11.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
Earlier fiscal, agricultural, maritime, provincial and social series

reports.title: Electricity generation by source / power-plant type
reports.publisher: BPS / Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources related
reports.description: Statistics on electricity production by generation type. Coal-fired (PLTU) remains dominant; gas, hydro, geothermal and other sources make up the balance. Total generation has been rising with demand.
reports._notes: Core power-mix node. Coal dominance is a central structural feature of the Indonesian energy system.
reports._url_evidence: BPS page confirms 'Statistik Listrik 2020-2024' from the Annual Survey of Electricity Companies: installed capacity, electricity produced and distributed.

reports.title: Energy Balance of Indonesia (detailed production–consumption)
reports.description: Official energy balance covering production through final consumption for oil, gas, coal and renewables. Extends the earlier Energy Balances node with fuller multi-year detail.
reports._notes: Comprehensive energy-flow node.
_referenced_by: Coal, oil and gas production series

reports.title: Crude oil and condensate production statistics
reports.publisher: BPS / Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources
reports.description: Long-run series of petroleum and condensate production. Shows the long-term decline from earlier peak levels; Indonesia is no longer a net oil exporter in the classic sense.
reports._notes: Declining-oil production node — important contrast with the still-large coal and gas roles.

reports.title: Natural gas production statistics
reports.publisher: BPS / Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources
reports.description: Natural gas production series (MMscf). Gas remains a significant domestic and export energy commodity and feeds both power generation and industrial use / LNG.
reports._notes: Gas-side counterpart to the oil and coal nodes.

reports.title: Religious composition statistics (Islam, Christianity, Hinduism, Buddhism, etc.)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Home Affairs (Dukcapil) / Population Census / BPS-related
reports.description: Official population statistics by religion. Islam constitutes the large majority (~87 %); Protestant, Catholic, Hindu, Buddhist, Confucian and other recognised categories make up the remainder. Continuously cited in social, cultural and political analysis.
reports._notes: Foundational social-identity node. Indonesia is the world’s largest Muslim-majority country; the official multi-religion statistics also capture significant Christian, Hindu and other communities.
_referenced_by: Regional cultural and political analysis (e.g. Bali Hindu concentration)
reports._url_evidence: Retrieved the BPS census portal table 'Penduduk Menurut Wilayah dan Agama yang Dianut, di INDONESIA' (Population by Region and Religion), Sensus Penduduk 2010, with figures rendering: Islam 104,528,568 (of a 237,641,326 total shown for the displayed breakdown), Kristen 7,118,678, Katolik 9,409,835, Hindu 2,418,492, Buddha 4,489,381, Khonghucu 117,091, Lainnya 139,582, plus urban/rural and sex disaggregation. Dukcapil publishes no religion-composition product; this BPS census table is the official statistical source.
reports._url_route: BPS subdomain sensus.bps.go.id (census tabular topic pages), found by searching the exact Indonesian table name

reports.title: Geographic distribution of religious communities
reports.publisher: Derived from census and civil-registration data
reports.description: Spatial patterning of religious affiliation — Muslim majority almost everywhere, with notable Hindu concentration in Bali, Christian majorities or large minorities in parts of eastern Indonesia (North Sulawesi, Papua, Maluku, NTT, etc.), and other local patterns.
reports._notes: Spatial densification of the religion cluster; links identity to the archipelagic geography already mapped.
_referenced_by: Provincial and Bali–Nusa Tenggara / Papua / Sulawesi nodes

reports.title: Geothermal power and renewable generation statistics
reports.publisher: BPS / Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources related
reports.description: Statistics on geothermal (PLTP) and other renewable generation. Indonesia has one of the world’s largest geothermal resource bases; actual generation remains a smaller but stable share of the mix.
reports._notes: Renewable-side densification of the energy cluster; geothermal is a distinctive Indonesian asset.
_referenced_by: Energy Balances and NDC / energy-transition documents
reports._url_evidence: MEMR page confirmed as the Handbook of Energy & Economic Statistics of Indonesia (HEESI) series, listing editions 2010-2025 covering energy supply including geothermal and renewables.

reports.title: Energy-transition and renewable-policy framing
reports.publisher: Government of Indonesia / MEMR / related planning documents
reports.description: Recurring policy framing around energy transition, renewable targets and the tension with continued coal dominance in the power sector. Continuously cited alongside NDC and long-term planning documents.
reports._notes: Policy-frame node for the energy-transition debate.
_referenced_by: Electricity mix, coal and GHG nodes

reports.title: Indonesia energy-mix–oil-gas–religion densification meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from BPS, MEMR, Dukcapil and related sources
reports.description: Meta-node binding electricity generation by source, detailed energy balances, oil and gas production, geothermal/renewables, energy-transition framing, religious composition and religious geography into a coherent energy-and-identity layer.
reports._notes: Integrating node for Batch 12 domains.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
Earlier coal, energy-balance, GHG, Islamic-finance and provincial series

reports.title: Tanjung Priok Port operational statistics
reports.description: Operational statistics for Indonesia’s principal container and logistics gateway port — vessel calls, container throughput (recently ~8.3 million TEUs), non-container cargo and related indicators. Central node in the national and international shipping system.
reports._notes: Primary international-gateway port node.
_referenced_by: Foreign trade and inter-island trade nodes
reports._url_evidence: BPS DKI Jakarta page confirms 'Statistik Transportasi Provinsi DKI Jakarta 2025' covering land, sea and air transport; the series is BPS's carrier for Tanjung Priok cargo and passenger data (port not named in the abstract itself).

reports.title: Tanjung Perak Port operational statistics
reports.description: Operational statistics for Tanjung Perak — major passenger and domestic-cargo hub in East Java. Frequently ranks among the busiest ports for inter-island passenger and cargo volumes.
reports._notes: Primary eastern-Java / domestic inter-island port node.
_referenced_by: Inter-island trade and East Java provincial nodes
reports._url_evidence: BPS East Java page confirms 'Statistik Transportasi Provinsi Jawa Timur 2023' presenting land, sea and air transport statistics for the province containing Tanjung Perak (port not named in the abstract itself).

reports.title: Major Indonesian ports system (Belawan, Makassar, and others)
reports.publisher: Pelindo / BPS / Ministry of Transportation related
reports.description: System-level view of the main commercial ports that handle the bulk of international and inter-island cargo and passengers. Complements the detailed Priok and Perak nodes and links to the chokepoint and connectivity layers.
reports._notes: Umbrella ports-system node.
_referenced_by: Tanjung Priok and Tanjung Perak nodes
reports._url_evidence: BPS page confirms 'Statistik Transportasi Laut 2024': vessel calls, cargo loading/unloading and passenger movements at seaports across 36 provinces.

reports.title: Profile of Ethnic Groups (Long Form Population Census 2020)
reports.description: Official socio-demographic profiles of major ethnic groups drawn from the Long Form SP2020 — age/sex composition, island distribution, concentration, fertility, marriage age, life expectancy, migration, education, and languages spoken. Captures the extreme ethnic diversity of the archipelago.
reports._notes: Foundational ethnic-diversity node. Complements the religious-composition series.
_referenced_by: Population Census and Long Form results

reports.title: Regional language diversity statistics (Long Form SP2020)
reports.description: Statistics on the use of regional languages within families and communities, and the diversity of local languages by island. Documents the linguistic plurality that sits alongside Indonesian as the national language.
reports._notes: Linguistic-diversity counterpart to the ethnic and religious nodes.

reports.title: Crime Statistics (Statistik Kriminal)
reports.publisher: BPS – Statistics Indonesia (Police registration + Susenas + Podes)
reports.description: Annual crime statistics combining police administrative records (crime total, crime rate, crime clock), Susenas victimisation data, and Village Potential (Podes) indicators of local crime incidence. Reporting rates to police remain relatively low.
reports._notes: Core security and justice statistical product.

reports.title: Crime victimisation and reporting-rate statistics
reports.publisher: BPS – Statistics Indonesia (Susenas component of Crime Statistics)
reports.description: Survey-based measures of the share of the population that experiences crime and the rate at which incidents are reported to the police. Complements the administrative crime-count series.
reports._notes: Victim-side densification of the security cluster.
reports._url_evidence: BPS page confirms 'Statistik Kriminal 2024/2025' and cites Susenas-based victimisation (0.73%) and crime reporting rate (20.28%) for 2024.

reports.title: Indonesia ports–ethnicity–language–crime densification meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from Pelindo, BPS Long Form and Crime Statistics sources
reports.description: Meta-node binding major port operational statistics (Tanjung Priok, Tanjung Perak, system), ethnic-group profiles, regional-language diversity, crime statistics and victimisation measures into a coherent infrastructure–identity–security layer.
reports._notes: Integrating node for Batch 13 domains.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
Earlier sea-transport, census, religious and provincial series

reports.title: BNPB – National Disaster Management Authority
reports.description: National focal point for disaster management, directly under the President. Coordinates risk reduction, preparedness, response and recovery. Publishes the integrated disaster data portal and the Indonesian Disaster Risk Index.
reports._notes: Institutional core of the disaster-management system.
_referenced_by: All disaster occurrence, risk-index and subnational BPBD series

reports.title: Disaster occurrence and impact statistics (by type and year)
reports.description: Compiled statistics on the number and impact of disasters by type (floods, landslides, earthquakes, tsunamis, volcanic eruptions, drought, extreme weather, coastal erosion, forest/peat fires, etc.) over multi-year periods.
reports._notes: Core empirical series for Indonesia’s high multi-hazard exposure.

reports.title: Indonesian Disaster Risk Index (IRBI)
reports.description: Composite index assessing disaster risk at provincial and district/city levels across major hazards. Used to prioritise Special Allocation Funds for disaster management and to guide local risk-reduction strategies.
reports._notes: Key spatial risk node that makes inter-regional differences in hazard exposure statistically explicit.
reports._url_evidence: BNPB product page confirms IRBI as the annual disaster risk index at district/city and provincial level (bnpb.go.id itself returns 403 to WebFetch).

reports.title: Provincial and local Disaster Management Agencies (BPBD)
reports.description: Subnational disaster-management agencies that implement risk reduction, preparedness and response at provincial and local levels. Coverage has expanded to nearly all provinces.
reports._notes: Subnational institutional densification of the disaster system.
_referenced_by: Disaster Risk Index and occurrence statistics

reports.title: Volcanic and earthquake / tsunami hazard and event statistics
reports.region: Especially Ring of Fire zones (Java, Sumatra, Sulawesi, eastern islands)
reports.description: Statistics and monitoring products focused on volcanic eruptions, earthquakes and tsunamis — the high-impact geophysical hazards that define much of Indonesia’s risk profile and have driven major policy redesigns (e.g. post-Palu tsunami warning improvements).
reports._notes: Geophysical-hazard densification. Indonesia sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire.
reports._url_evidence: Confirmed as PVMBG (Center for Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation, Badan Geologi ESDM), publishing daily volcano status/alert levels, seismic counts and eruption observations.

reports.title: National disaster-management policy and legal framework
reports.description: Legal and policy instruments governing disaster management (including the post-2004 institutional redesign that created BNPB and the subsequent risk-reduction strategies). Recurring citation in resilience and development planning.
reports._notes: Policy-frame node for the entire disaster cluster.
_referenced_by: BNPB, BPBD and Risk Index nodes

reports.title: Indonesia disaster-risk and management meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from BNPB and related sources
reports.description: Meta-node binding BNPB, disaster occurrence/impact statistics, Disaster Risk Index, BPBD subnational system, volcano/earthquake/tsunami focus, and the national policy framework into a coherent multi-hazard resilience layer with explicit inter-regional variation.
reports._notes: Integrating node for the disaster round.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch

reports.title: Indonesia–Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (IJEPA)
reports.description: Indonesia’s first bilateral EPA. Covers goods, services, investment and capacity building. Continuously cited in Japan–Indonesia trade and investment analysis.
reports._notes: Foundational bilateral EPA node with Japan.
_referenced_by: Foreign trade and FDI statistics (Japan partner share)
reports._url_evidence: Ministry of Trade DG for International Trade Negotiations page describes IJEPA: signed 2007, in force 1 July 2008, scope and general review.

reports.title: ASEAN–Australia–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (AANZFTA)
reports.description: Multilateral FTA between ASEAN and Australia/New Zealand covering goods, services and investment. Part of the broader ASEAN+ network.
reports._notes: ASEAN+ Oceania trade-architecture node.
reports._url_evidence: Official AANZFTA site overview page lists the twelve parties including Indonesia and the agreement's goods/services/investment coverage.

reports.title: Indonesia–Australia Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (IA-CEPA)
reports.description: Bilateral comprehensive partnership covering goods, services, investment and temporary movement of persons.
reports._notes: Bilateral Australia CEPA node.
_referenced_by: Trade and FDI statistics with Australia
reports._url_evidence: Australian DFAT in-force agreements page for IA-CEPA, describing the bilateral framework, trade figures and the skills-exchange pilot.

reports.title: Indonesia–EU Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (IEU-CEPA)
reports.description: Comprehensive trade agreement covering the large majority of tariff lines. Negotiations concluded; entry into force pending ratification (targeted around 2027 in recent reporting).
reports._notes: Major prospective European trade-architecture node.
reports._url_evidence: European Commission DG Trade page confirms the EU-Indonesia CEPA: negotiations launched 2016, concluded 23 September 2025, plus the Investment Protection Agreement.

reports.title: Bilateral Investment Treaty (BIT) network
reports.publisher: Government of Indonesia / UNCTAD navigator compilations
reports.description: Indonesia’s stock of bilateral investment treaties (in force, signed, terminated). Provides the legal infrastructure for investment protection and is continuously referenced in FDI and investor-state analysis.
reports._notes: Umbrella investment-treaty network node.

reports.title: Energy Balances of Indonesia

reports.title: Producer Price Index / Wholesale Price statistics
reports.description: Producer and wholesale price indices that complement the CPI and feed into national-accounts deflators and industrial cost analysis.

reports.title: Agricultural statistics (production, food crops, estate crops)
reports.publisher: BPS – Statistics Indonesia / Ministry of Agriculture related
reports.description: Recurring statistics on food-crop and estate-crop production (including palm oil, rubber, cocoa, etc.), livestock and related agricultural indicators. Central to both domestic food security and major export commodities.

reports.title: Health and vital statistics (beyond census)

reports.title: Palm-oil production and estate-crop statistics

reports.title: Nickel and downstream mineral statistics

reports.title: Coal production and export statistics
reports.publisher: BPS / Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources related

reports.title: Mining and quarrying statistics (broader)

reports.title: DKI Jakarta – capital special region

reports.title: Internal migration and urbanisation statistics

reports.title: Informal employment proportion statistics (by province)
reports.description: Official Sakernas-based statistics on the share of informal employment. National figure remains high (around 58 % in recent data); provincial variation is large, with eastern and rural provinces showing much higher informality.
reports._notes: Critical structural labour node. High informality is a defining feature of the Indonesian labour market.

reports.title: Micro and small manufacturing industry statistics
reports.description: Statistics on the number and characteristics of micro and small manufacturing establishments by province. Complements the large-and-medium manufacturing series and highlights the vast MSME base, especially on Java.
reports._notes: MSME densification of the industrial cluster.

reports.title: Broader MSME / micro-enterprise statistics and policy framing
reports.publisher: BPS / Ministry of Cooperatives and SMEs / related
reports.description: Official and quasi-official statistics and policy framing around micro, small and medium enterprises more broadly (beyond manufacturing). Continuously cited in employment, inclusion and recovery narratives.
reports._notes: Umbrella MSME node.
reports._url_evidence: Retrieved the BPS booklet 'Potensi Usaha Mikro Kecil' from the 2016 Economic Census follow-up (data collected 2017). Confirmed content: 26+ million micro and small enterprises = 98.68% of all non-agricultural businesses, employing 59 million workers (75.33% of the non-agricultural workforce); covers 16 non-agricultural sectors - trade ~50%, food and accommodation >16%, manufacturing >16%, plus construction, transport, education, health and finance - with 43% of proprietors female and only 12% accessing formal credit. This is the broader, cross-sector MSME product the item asks for. kemenkopukm.go.id and satudata.kemenkopukm.go.id still fail TLS/robots checks; BPS's national 'Profil Industri Mikro dan Kecil 2024' (https://www.bps.go.id/id/publication/2025/09/16/a83f105e49377d0a7434e62a/profil-industri-mikro-dan-kecil-2024.html) also loads but is manufacturing-only.
reports._url_route: BPS census subdomain se2016.bps.go.id static file path, after the Ministry of Cooperatives and SMEs hosts stayed TLS-blocked

reports.title: Nusantara Capital City (IKN) legal and planning framework

reports.title: Foreign-exchange reserves statistics

reports.title: Labour productivity and related indicators

reports.title: Financial-inclusion statistics

reports.title: Statistics of Marine and Coastal Resources
reports.description: Annual BPS publication on the potential and management of marine and coastal resources. Framed around blue-economy, climate adaptation and sustainable coastal prosperity themes aligned with long-term national planning.

reports.title: Statistics of Fishing Ports
reports.description: Annual statistics on the number, class and activity of fishing ports, fish-auction facilities and related catch volumes handled through ports. Aceh and other provinces feature prominently in port counts.
reports._notes: Infrastructure and production node for the capture-fisheries sector.

reports.title: Fisheries production statistics (capture and aquaculture)
reports.publisher: BPS / Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries related
reports.description: Official statistics on fish catch and aquaculture production. Indonesia ranks among the world’s largest fisheries producers; the series is central to food security, exports and coastal livelihoods.
reports._notes: Primary production node for the maritime food economy.

reports.title: Kota Magelang / Kabupaten Magelang local statistics (Dalam Angka)
reports.publisher: BPS Kota Magelang / BPS Kabupaten Magelang
reports.description: Annual ‘Dalam Angka’ (in figures) publications for Magelang City and Magelang Regency. Standard local statistical yearbooks covering population, labour, social, economic and regional-account indicators. Magelang sits in the Central Java highland corridor.
reports._notes: Local node with historical continuity. Magelang was a Dutch East Indies administrative posting; it remains an active BPS statistical unit today.

_consolidation.json_syntax_repair_note: These batch files were not valid JSON as delivered: "releases_per_year" carried an unquoted text value (missing opening quote), e.g. `"releases_per_year": continuous",`. Repaired mechanically by re-quoting the value verbatim. No number was invented.
_consolidation.cadence_note: A non-numeric cadence text was moved off releases_per_year into _cadence_original verbatim and the numeric field omitted, per the v2 spec (omitted, never null). Needs a human/judgement pass to become a real number.

_normalisation.note: Second pass, 2026-08-18: mechanical alignment to src/lib/types.ts. Nothing researched, nothing invented. Every original value that was replaced is preserved on the record under a key prefixed with an underscore.
rules: jurisdiction_level mapped into the six-value union; the delivered string kept as _jurisdiction_level_original.
domains: format-normalised, then any tag outside the 22 approved values prefixed "proposed:" as the spec directs. No semantic merging was done — that needs your call.

relationship_type: part_of edges moved onto the child node as part_of; contains edges reversed onto the child; produced_by edges dropped (publisher is a string, not a node); related_to / complements held in _dropped as deferred. Off-union values were poisoning every PageRank score with NaN.
last_updated added as null where absent (required field, string|null).
region filled with the country name where it was null or missing.
releases_per_year: unambiguous single-word cadences resolved to numbers; ambiguous text left in _cadence_original and listed under _gaps.unresolved_cadence.
source_kind mapped to official/commercial; delivered value kept as _source_kind_original.
Non-schema keys Grok wrote (shape, notes, referenced_by, ...) renamed with a leading underscore so they are visibly not part of the schema. Nothing deleted.

_gaps.note: What is genuinely missing and cannot be fixed mechanically — this is the research queue, not a defect list.

url_research_pass.method: Per-country web research. A URL was accepted only when the page was actually retrieved and its content confirmed the publication. Publisher homepages, Wikipedia, news, aggregators and mirrors were rejected. Confirmations are stored on each node as _url_evidence.
